inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E AUTOMOTIVE net sales (GMNA + GMI + Corporate), i.e. consolidated revenue less the GM Financial segment. TTM to 30-Sep-2026 automotive revenue is $169.8B (consolidated $186.95B less GMF $17.16B); FY2026E ~$171B allows a normal Q4. GM Financial is valued in the equity bridge, not in the flows, so its $17B of revenue is excluded from the base.
inputs.share_count_basis: 843.5M basic shares at 9-Oct-2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover) plus 15M dilutive effect of stock incentive awards (Q3 2026 diluted EPS table) = 858.5M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Buybacks ($5.3B in 9M-2026, $6.0B FY2025, new $20B authorization) are value-neutral in this model; they are the mechanism funding the flat count.
inputs.net_debt_note: AUTOMOTIVE only, 30-Sep-2026: automotive cash and cash equivalents $18.8B + marketable debt securities $4.4B = $23.1B, less total automotive debt $15.8B (incl. finance leases) = net cash $7.3B. GM Financial's $112.9B of secured/unsecured debt is EXCLUDED: it funds finance receivables and leased vehicles and is serviced by GMF's own earnings; GMF is carried in the equity bridge at an equity value instead. Treating GMF debt as GM net debt would wipe out the equity and is the classic captive-finance error.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: TTM to 30-Sep-2026 automotive free cash flow BEFORE management-action adjustments and EXCLUDING GM Financial dividends: automotive OCF $19.3B (FY2025 $18.7B + 9M-2026 $13.7B - 9M-2025 $13.1B) less capex $8.9B (9.2 + 5.8 - 6.1) = $10.4B, less GMF dividends received $1.6B (1.5 + 1.2 - 1.1, which sit inside automotive OCF but are valued via the bridge) = $8.8B. GM's own 'adjusted automotive FCF' adds back $4.2B of 9M-2026 management actions (EV realignment supplier settlements, Cruise wind-down) and is guided $11.5-12.5B for FY2026; the owner basis here does not add those back.
inputs.mid_cycle_fcf_note: Sanity-check fix (Step 8c.5 item 1). Owner automotive FCF history FY2021-FY2025 ($B): -1.7, 7.4, 6.9, 10.1, 6.8; median 6.9. Latest (TTM Sep-2026) 7.6. Mid-point of median and latest = $7.25B, SBC-adjusted throughout. The base-case driver paths are set so that year-1 (FY2027) owner FCF lands at ~$7.3B and the ten-year series hovers $6.8-7.7B instead of climbing from $8.0B to $10.1B as the pre-fix base did. This is implemented through the EBITDA margin path (11.2% -> 10.5% mid-cycle) and a 1.5% growth cap, not by overriding last_fcf, so the engine's component build stays auditable.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K consolidated cash-flow statement / XBRL ShareBasedCompensation: $334M (FY2024 $332M, FY2023 $340M). GM publishes no separate equity-award tax line (share withholding is netted inside 'Other financing activities'), so the cash-flow add-back is used; at 0.2% of revenue the difference is immaterial.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 automotive interest income $854M (EBIT-adjusted reconciliation). Stripped from owner FCF because the automotive cash pile and the Ultium loan that earn it are added in the bridge. Automotive interest EXPENSE ($727M FY2025) is left inside last_fcf (OCF is post-interest), which makes the audit anchor slightly conservative versus the pre-interest component build.
inputs.buyback_note: 9M-2026 payments to purchase common stock $5,301M (FY2025 $6,012M; FY2024 $7,064M; FY2023 $11,115M). The $6B January-2026 program is complete; a new $20B authorization (no expiry) was approved 20-Oct-2026. Authorized is not spent; only the financing-activity outflow is recorded here.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. BASE: 10-year UST ~4.2% + equity risk premium 5.0% x beta ~1.2 for a US volume automaker = ~10.0% cost of equity; the automotive business is net cash so WACC = cost of equity. PREMIUMS added in the 2026-11-08 sanity-check fix (research-stock Step 8c.5 item 2 template, low end of each band because the probability-weighted bear case already carries a recession in the flows and the method's rule (f) says risk should be charged once): (i) extreme cyclicality +1.0% (GM's EBIT-adjusted swung from deeply negative in 2008-09 to +$14-15B; GMNA margin ranges 5-10% across a cycle, far more than 3x peak-to-trough at the EBIT line); (ii) regulatory / trade-policy single point of failure +1.0% (Section 232/USMCA tariffs of $2.5-3.5B/yr, CAFE and emissions-credit rules and the China JV licence all sit with a handful of government decisions; the tariff COST is in the flows, the premium prices the unhedgeable policy variance). Small-cap illiquidity is not applicable (large cap). WACC = 12.0%, held identical across all three scenarios so the bear is not charged a third time through the rate. Acknowledged overlap: a mid-cycle base, a 30% recession-bear weight and a cyclicality premium together are deliberately conservative; the sensitivity grid shows the 10% row for the risk-in-flows-only reading.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease cost is already an operating expense inside EBIT-adjusted (treatment B for operating leases) and finance leases are inside 'total automotive debt' (treatment A). Nothing is deducted twice: no lease_cost_pct_path is modelled, and lease liabilities are not added to net debt beyond the finance leases GM itself reports in automotive debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: GM's EBIT-adjusted is presented net of noncontrolling interests ($1.7B NCI equity at 30-Sep-2026, mostly GM Korea preferred and SGMW-related). Because the margin path is anchored to that attributable measure, the flows are already attributable-only and NO NCI deduction is made in the bridge (charge once).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF on the AUTOMOTIVE business (GMNA + GMI + Corporate) with GM Financial, the pension/OPEB deficit and the Ultium loan receivable handled in the equity bridge. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: operating company, cyclical US industrial, so owner-fcf.md plus the adaptations file (captive-finance arm treated like an embedded lender: its debt is operating funding and is excluded from net debt; its equity value is added to EV; its dividend to the parent is stripped from automotive flows so it is not counted twice). First valuation of GM in this folder (no MEMORY entry). SCOPE OF THE FLOWS: EBITDA margin is pre-SBC automotive EBIT-adjusted (which includes equity income from the China JVs and Ultium Cells, net of NCI) plus automotive D&A; the engine then deducts SBC, D&A, cash tax, capex. Equity income stays in the flows, so the $5.4B carrying value of nonconsolidated affiliates is NOT added to the bridge (matching-asset rule). Automotive interest income is excluded from EBIT-adjusted by definition, and the cash and Ultium loan that earn it are in the bridge. FY0 is FY2026E (nine months reported; the balance-sheet anchors are 30-Sep-2026, so Q4-2026 FCF, which guidance implies is roughly nil, is simply omitted). Price is the 6-Nov-2026 regular close, not an after-hours print. Cash tax starts well below the 20-21% ETR-adjusted guidance because GM's US deferred tax assets held cash taxes to $1.5-1.7B/yr (10-13% of adjusted pre-tax) in FY2023-FY2025; the path ramps to the 21% statutory-equivalent rate over five years rather than perpetuating the shelter. SANITY-CHECK FIX 2026-11-08: the first build tripped sanity_check.py on implied P/E 51.5x vs a 10.3x ten-year average. Two causes, one artefact. Causes fixed: (1) the base case extrapolated FY2026 guidance, GM's highest EBIT-adjusted year on record, flat for ten years with no downturn, growing 2-2.5%/yr; rebuilt on mid-cycle owner FCF (see mid_cycle_fcf) and growth capped at the through-cycle automotive revenue CAGR of ~1.5% (FY2010 $135.3B -> FY2025 $167.8B ex-GMF). (2) WACC carried no cyclicality or policy premium; +2.0% added (see wacc_rationale). Artefact that remains: the check divides base IV by FY2025 SBC-adjusted GAAP EPS of $2.51, a year carrying ~$7B of EV-realignment and China charges (EPS-diluted-adjusted was ~$10.5); the current share price is itself 34x that denominator, so no defensible model clears the 20.7x line on it. The honest test is implied P/E on normalised mid-cycle earnings, recorded in valuation_philosophy.

equity_bridge.item: GM Financial equity value (~1.0x estimated book)
equity_bridge.note: GMF is wholly owned and consolidated; GM's 10-K/10-Q disclose GMF segment total assets $139.3B and GMF debt $112.9B at 30-Sep-2026 but not GMF equity directly. GMF's own 10-K equity has run ~$14-16B (earning assets ~$120B at a ~7.5-8x leverage ratio); after deferred-tax and payable liabilities the implied book is ~$15-16B. $15.0B is the conservative end of that range and also ~7x GMF's after-tax EBT-adjusted (FY2025 $2.8B pre-tax, 9M-2026 $1.96B), where listed auto lenders such as Ally trade. GMF's $1.2-1.5B annual dividend to GM is excluded from automotive flows so this value is not double counted.

equity_bridge.item: Pension and OPEB deficit, after tax
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 10-K funded status 31-Dec-2025: US pension -$657M, non-US pension -$2,929M, global OPEB -$4,372M = -$7,958M; x (1 - 21%) = -$6,285M. Deducted as debt-like because EBIT-adjusted carries almost no pension/OPEB P&L cost (net pension/OPEB expense $29M FY2025) while cash contributions and OPEB benefit payments run ~$0.5B/yr; the deficit is the PV of those excess cash outflows, so charging it here and not in the margin is a single charge.

equity_bridge.item: Ultium Cells LLC term loan receivable
equity_bridge.note: $1.8B 5.7% term loan advanced May-2025 (matures Apr-2030), $0.4B repaid FY2025 and $0.2B in 9M-2026; ~$1.2B outstanding. Its interest is inside the automotive interest income excluded from the flows, so the asset belongs in the bridge.

historical_growth.revenue_through_cycle_note: First-to-last year of the data (Step 8c.5 item 3): consolidated FY2010 $135.6B -> FY2025 $185.0B over 15 years = 2.1%/yr, but that includes GM Financial growing from ~$0.3B (AmeriCredit acquired Oct-2010) to $17.2B. Automotive only: ~$135.3B -> $167.8B = 1.45%/yr; from the FY2011 post-bankruptcy recovery year it is below 1%. Base-case growth and terminal growth are capped at 1.5%.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: through-cycle automotive revenue CAGR FY2010-FY2025 (~1.5%), per the sanity-check fix; the 3- and 5-year CAGRs measure the post-COVID recovery window and are not usable as a forward rate (see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR (4.9%) sits 43% below revenue 5-yr CAGR (8.6%); equity 3-yr CAGR is negative (-4.2%) because $24B of buybacks in FY2023-FY2025 shrank book equity while the FY2024 China impairment and FY2025 EV realignment charges hit retained earnings. GAAP EPS CAGRs are dominated by those charges (FY2025 GAAP EPS $3.33 vs EPS-diluted-adjusted ~$10.5). Neither is a growth signal; forward growth is set from the through-cycle revenue CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are consolidated (FY2020 $122.5B COVID base -> FY2025 $185.0B; FY2022 $156.7B -> FY2025). Owner automotive FCF series (automotive OCF - capex - GMF dividends - SBC - automotive interest income, $B): FY2021 -1.7 (chip-shortage working-capital drain, $3.5B GMF dividend), FY2022 7.4, FY2023 6.9, FY2024 10.1, FY2025 6.8; 3-yr CAGR FY2022->FY2025 -2.8% versus reported automotive FCF (OCF - capex) 10.0 -> 9.5, -1.7%. The gap is rising interest income on the cash pile, not SBC (flat at ~$0.33B). A 5-yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined because the FY2021 base is negative. TTM to Sep-2026 owner FCF $7.6B is depressed by $4.2B of EV-realignment and Cruise cash costs.

base.growth_note: Capped at the through-cycle automotive revenue CAGR (~1.5%, FY2010-FY2025) per the sanity-check fix; pre-fix path was 2.0-2.5%. US industry ~16M SAAR flat, GM share 16-17%, price/mix +1-2%, GMI low single digits, less a normal share of downturn years.
base.ebitda_margin_note: MID-CYCLE pre-SBC automotive EBITDA, not FY2026 guidance. FY2026E guidance implies ~11.5% (automotive EBIT-adjusted ~$12.4B + D&A $6.9B + SBC $0.3B on $171B), GM's best year on record; the pre-fix base held 11.6-11.8% for ten years. The fix glides from 11.2% in FY2027 to 10.5% from FY2029, i.e. automotive EBIT-adjusted ~6.2% = GMNA ~8% (bottom of the 8-10% target band, which is where a blended cycle lands once one downturn year in ten is averaged in) + GMI ~3% + Corporate drag + China JV equity income. Year-1 owner FCF ~$7.3B ties to mid_cycle_fcf; the series then runs $6.8-7.7B through 2036.
base.capex_note: Includes capital contributions to the battery JVs (~0.5% of revenue) on top of the reported capex line (FY2025 $9.2B = 5.5%; 9M-2026 $5.8B). GM guides $10-12B of 'capital spending and investments in battery cell JVs' for 2026; the $5B onshoring programme (Tennessee, Kansas, Michigan, New York V8) runs through 2027-28, after which capex settles at ~1.1pp above D&A.
base.cash_tax_note: Cash taxes paid FY2023-FY2025 of $1.5-1.7B were 10-13% of adjusted pre-tax income thanks to US deferred tax assets; ramped to 21% by year 5 rather than perpetuating the shelter. ETR-adjusted (book) guidance is 20-21%.
base.terminal_note: Exit-multiple cap (Step 8c.5 item 4) expressed in owner-FCF terms because no historical EV/EBITDA series exists for GM (GMF's leased-vehicle depreciation makes consolidated EBITDA meaningless). 10x mid-cycle owner FCF of ~$7.7B is ~$77B of terminal EV; on normalised mid-cycle net income of ~$8.5-10B (consolidated EBIT-adjusted ~$13B less 21% tax less SBC) that is ~8-9x earnings, inside GM's 10.3x ten-year average P/E and well under the 15-20x P/E ceiling (1.5-2x the average) the fix allows. Gordon at 12%/1.5% implies 9.7x, so the cap no longer binds; it is the backstop.

bull.note: Trimmed in the fix: margin plateau 13.0% -> 12.2% (GMNA sustained at ~9.5%, top of band, no downturn in ten years) and growth 3.5/3.0 -> 3.0/2.5 fading to 2.0. The 12x owner-FCF exit is ~11x normalised earnings, GM's ten-year average P/E of 10.3x with a modest re-rating, inside the 15-20x ceiling.

bear.note: Flows unchanged by the fix: the bear already carried a 2028 recession and GM's historical 8x exit. Only the WACC moved, to the same 12% as the other scenarios.

scenario_narratives.base: MID-CYCLE case, not a guidance extrapolation. US industry averages ~16M SAAR across the decade with a normal share of soft years blended in; automotive revenue grows at the through-cycle 1.5%. GMNA averages ~8% EBIT-adjusted, the bottom of management's 8-10% band, because FY2026-27 run near the top of the band and a downturn year somewhere in the window pulls the average down; tariffs persist at $2.5-3.5B/yr, offset by shrinking EV losses, onshoring and cost discipline. GMI low single digits, SAIC-GM equity income modest. Capex stays elevated through the 2027-28 onshoring and battery-JV commitments then settles ~1pp above D&A. Cash tax ramps from the DTA-sheltered ~14% to 21%. Owner FCF runs $6.8-7.7B a year, in line with the FY2022-FY2025 median and the TTM. Exit 10x owner FCF (~9x normalised earnings), inside GM's own history.
scenario_narratives.bull: Tariff relief (refunds, USMCA clarity, Section 232 exemptions) and full-size truck/SUV strength hold GMNA at the top of the 8-10% band for the whole decade with no downturn, EV losses fall away and Super Cruise/OnStar software revenue scales; China JV equity income recovers toward $1B; GMI holds 5-6%. Automotive revenue grows 2.5-3% early on share gains and mix. Capex normalises faster to 5% of revenue once onshoring completes. The market grants a 12x owner-FCF exit (~11x normalised earnings) as the EV/China/Cruise overhangs stay in the rearview mirror and buybacks retire ~7% of the count a year.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2028 US downturn: industry SAAR falls to ~13.5M, automotive revenue drops ~14% over two years, and GM's high fixed cost base takes GMNA toward 5-6% (automotive EBITDA 7.5-8%) with incentives rising and used-vehicle residuals pressuring GMF. Tariffs stay at the top of the range or widen, EV supplier settlements keep generating 'special' cash costs, and the China JV stalls again under BYD-led price competition. Capex cannot flex below ~6% because the onshoring and battery commitments are contracted. Margins recover only to 10% EBITDA (GMNA ~7.5%) by 2031 and the exit stays at GM's historical 8x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged by the sanity-check fix. Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: GM is a high-fixed-cost cyclical seven years into a US auto expansion, with tariff policy, EV economics and the China JV all still open. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance has been raised twice and the EV capacity reassessment is complete, so the central path is well anchored (now as a mid-cycle average rather than a guidance run-rate). Bull cut to 20% because it needs tariff relief, a China recovery and a sustained multiple re-rating to happen together. Weights sum to 1.0. Note the overlap with the WACC cyclicality premium, acknowledged in wacc_rationale.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the automotive business on MID-CYCLE owner free cash flow (pre-SBC EBITDA gliding from near-guidance 11.2% to a through-cycle 10.5%, less SBC, cash tax ramping to statutory, capex including battery-JV contributions, revenue growing at the through-cycle 1.5%) and add the pieces that sit outside those flows: automotive net cash, GM Financial at roughly book, the Ultium loan, less the after-tax pension/OPEB deficit. GM Financial's debt is operating funding for a lender and is never treated as GM net debt. Discount at 12%: a 10% automaker cost of equity plus explicit +1% cyclicality and +1% trade/regulatory-policy premiums. Exit multiples are held at GM's own history (8/10/12x owner FCF, roughly 7/9/11x normalised earnings) rather than the method's 12-15x cyclical band. The result is a stock trading near its probability-weighted value at the 96th percentile of its ten-year price range: an income-plus-buyback compounder at a fair price, not a multi-bagger, with the bear case roughly 30% below the price.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_fix: WHAT TRIPPED: scripts/sanity_check.py flagged the first build's base IV ($129.45) at an implied 51.5x P/E against GM's 10.3x ten-year average (never above 32x). WHAT CHANGED (research-stock Step 8c.5, in priority order): (1) peak-earnings extrapolation fixed: the base case had held FY2026 guidance, GM's highest EBIT-adjusted year on record (11.6-11.8% automotive EBITDA margin), flat for ten years with no downturn; rebuilt on mid-cycle owner FCF of ~$7.3B (mid-point of the FY2021-25 median $6.9B and the TTM $7.6B, SBC-adjusted throughout) via a 10.5% mid-cycle margin, with growth capped at the through-cycle automotive revenue CAGR of 1.5% (pre-fix 2.0-2.5%); the bull plateau was trimmed from 13.0% to 12.2%. (2) WACC understatement fixed: +1.0% extreme-cyclicality and +1.0% regulatory/trade-policy premiums added to the 10% cost of equity = 12%, applied identically to all three scenarios, each documented in inputs.wacc_rationale. (3) Exit cap: no historical EV/EBITDA exists for GM (GMF depreciation pollutes consolidated EBITDA), so the P/E-based cyclical cap is used: terminal multiples of 8/10/12x owner FCF equal ~7/9/11x normalised mid-cycle earnings, under the 15-20x P/E ceiling (1.5-2x the 10.3x average); Gordon at 12% now sits below the caps so they are backstops. RESULTING MULTIPLES: see reconciliation and the sanity_check block's implied_multiples_after_fix. The check's P/E denominator is FY2025 SBC-adjusted GAAP EPS of $2.51, a year carrying ~$7B of EV-realignment and China charges (adjusted EPS ~$10.5); the market price itself is 34x that figure, so the mechanical rule cannot clear 20.7x on any defensible value. On normalised mid-cycle earnings ($8.5-10B attributable after SBC, i.e. $9.9-11.7/share on 858.5M shares: automotive EBIT-adjusted ~$10.8B at the 10.5% mid-cycle margin plus GMF ~$2.5B, less 21% tax and SBC, with the low end allowing a GMF credit cycle) the post-fix base IV of $94.29 is 8.1-9.5x and the weighted IV of $93.89 is 8.0-9.5x, inside the 10.3x ten-year average; P/B and P/Sales were already inside their historical maxima and move lower. INVESTMENT FRAMING: GM is a mid-cycle, high-fixed-cost automaker at a cyclical high in both earnings and share price; the model now says fairly valued to modestly cheap, with the 15% hurdle entry price well below the market. The thesis is capital return (buybacks retiring ~6-7% of shares a year on a ~9x adjusted P/E) rather than growth or re-rating.
key_risks_to_valuation: GM Financial equity value is estimated (~$15B) from GM's segment disclosures and GMF's historical leverage, not read from GMF's standalone 10-K; a +/-$3B error is +/-$3.5/share. Residual-value or credit losses in a downturn would cut it further.

Cyclical volume: every 1M units of US SAAR is roughly $1.5-2B of GMNA EBIT; the base now averages one soft patch into its margin and the bear models an explicit 2028 recession; a 2008-style collapse would push value below the bear figure.

Risk charged more than once: the mid-cycle base, the 30% recession-bear weight and the +2% WACC premium overlap; the 10% WACC row of the sensitivity grid is the risk-in-flows-only reading and is materially higher.
Tariffs are modelled as a persistent $2.5-3.5B/yr cost; policy can move either way with little notice.

Cash tax ramp: the model assumes the US deferred-tax shelter unwinds by 2031; if credits persist longer the value is understated, if they are impaired (e.g. emissions-credit write-offs up to $1.1B) cash tax rises sooner.

Exit multiple: GM has rarely traded above 8x FCF; the base case's 10x cap and the bull's 12x are mild re-rating assumptions. At GM's historical 7x the base value is materially lower (see required-return table and sensitivity grid).
EV realignment and China 'special' cash costs ($4.2B in 9M-2026, $1.1B FY2025) are treated as non-recurring beyond FY2026; if they recur annually the owner FCF base is ~$1-2B/yr lower.
Pension/OPEB deficit is sensitive to discount rates: a 1pp fall in rates adds several $B to the $8B deficit.
